A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, framework and principal experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy-model training, leave-one-out and temporal-ablation experiments, Pythia token-influence analyses, and an induction-head formation experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical studies and adds delimiter-subtype analyses and a controlled experiment intervening in induction-head formation.

M1.justification: The BIF definition, RMSPropSGLD estimator, localization, per-token computation and normalization remain unchanged. The new loss-upweighting experiment tests the framework rather than modifying the proposed attribution procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions study the hierarchical semantic dataset, structural tokens from The Pile and synthetic repeated-token sequences. V2 subdivides existing delimiter categories and intervenes in the existing induction-learning task; these additions do not introduce a new domain or task.

E2.justification: The new intervention comparison in Appendix D.4 includes unweighted training and alternative upweighting windows as comparators. Existing LOO and damped classical-IF comparisons remain. The added discussion of EK-FAC does not constitute an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a controlled training protocol: a 3-million-parameter transformer, 13 million Pile sequences, 15,000 steps, and fourfold induction-token loss weighting during six listed 500-step windows, with initialization and data order held fixed. Appendix D.2 adds delimiter-subtype grouping and mixed-delimiter filtering. Existing hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices D.2 and D.4 test fine-grained delimiter relationships and whether intervention timing causally changes induction-head formation. These substantially extend the language-model analyses. The toy-model temporal ablation in C.5 and the earlier induction-tracking study were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Figure 17 introduces a 90% confidence band using a 100-sample block bootstrap of the approximate posterior. This is new uncertainty reporting, but it does not establish repeated training across independent seeds. Existing sampler-chain counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds delimiter-subtype trajectories and intervention results showing accelerated induction for later windows and delayed or suppressed induction for early windows. Section 4 changes the reported induction onset from 1,000 to 128 steps and opposite-delimiter influence from increasingly negative to increasingly positive. Analytical curves in Figure 3 are also revised; v1 Figure 15 is retained as v2 Figure 16.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 replaces the singular-vector perturbation formulas in v1 Equations 50–51 with coupled terms over squared singular-value gaps in v2 Equations 48–49. It also repairs indices in the loss expansion. These are localized mathematical revisions; the main SLT and covariance-decomposition arguments remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions and concluding argument retain the same central claims: stagewise influence, analytical and empirical toy-model validation, and corresponding language-model phenomena. The new experiments support these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies total-influence peaks as conditional, discusses possible cancellation of signed influence in unrolling methods, and explains BIF's setup-cost versus per-query-cost tradeoff. It interprets the new intervention as evidence for timing-dependent receptivity. The stated Bayesian-to-SGD theoretical gap remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices D.2 and D.4 document delimiter filtering and the new intervention's model size, data quantity, budget, weighting factor and timing controls. Existing sampler details remain. One new inconsistency limits precision: D.4 says five experimental runs but lists and plots six intervention windows.

R1.justification: V2 adds Stewart and Sun's Matrix Perturbation Theory as support for the SVD derivation. It also expands positioning against unrolling-based attribution and discusses computational tradeoffs against EK-FAC, while retaining the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the causal-validation explanation, revise the language-model narrative and discussion, and repair wording and cross-references. Appendix D gains two subsections and renames the retained induction study. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout throughout, changing margins, typography and figure placement. Figure 5 is redrawn with logarithmic checkpoints; the toy appendix plots are reassigned or replaced to match their captions. New Figures 15 and 17 are added, while the earlier induction figure becomes Figure 16.

improvement.justification: The controlled language-model intervention adds useful causal support beyond v1's toy ablation, while corrected plot-caption correspondence and qualified theoretical interpretation improve clarity. These are bounded gains: the central framework and theoretical limitations remain, and the new bootstrap band does not establish robustness across training seeds.
